title: Sudoku Solver
description:
# Sudoku Solver

Write a program that solves a Sudoku puzzle by filling every empty cell in place.

A valid Sudoku solution must satisfy all of these rules:

1. Each digit `1` through `9` appears exactly once in every row.
2. Each digit `1` through `9` appears exactly once in every column.
3. Each digit `1` through `9` appears exactly once in every `3 x 3` sub-box.

The character `'.'` marks an empty cell. The input board is guaranteed to have exactly one solution. Your method should mutate `board` to that solved grid and does not need to return anything.

The nine boxes are fixed disjoint `3 x 3` regions, each covering three consecutive rows and columns and together covering the board. Preserve all prefilled digits.

## Example 1:

**Input:** board = [["5","3",".",".","7",".",".",".","."],["6",".",".","1","9","5",".",".","."],[".","9","8",".",".",".",".","6","."],["8",".",".",".","6",".",".",".","3"],["4",".",".","8",".","3",".",".","1"],["7",".",".",".","2",".",".",".","6"],[".","6",".",".",".",".","2","8","."],[".",".",".","4","1","9",".",".","5"],[".",".",".",".","8",".",".","7","9"]]
**Output:** [["5","3","4","6","7","8","9","1","2"],["6","7","2","1","9","5","3","4","8"],["1","9","8","3","4","2","5","6","7"],["8","5","9","7","6","1","4","2","3"],["4","2","6","8","5","3","7","9","1"],["7","1","3","9","2","4","8","5","6"],["9","6","1","5","3","7","2","8","4"],["2","8","7","4","1","9","6","3","5"],["3","4","5","2","8","6","1","7","9"]]

## Constraints:

* `board.length == 9`
* `board[i].length == 9`
* `board[i][j]` is a digit from `'1'` to `'9'` or `'.'`
* The input board has exactly one solution.

solutions.name: Plain Backtracking with Board Scan
solutions.timeComplexity: O(9^E), where E is the number of empty cells
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan the board to find the first empty cell, try digits `1` through `9`, and accept a digit only if the row, column, and `3 x 3` box remain valid. If later recursion fails, restore the cell to `'.'` and try the next digit.

## Key Insight

This version mirrors the Sudoku rules directly. It is slower because every candidate performs a row, column, and box scan, but it is the clearest correctness baseline.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(9^E), where E is the number of empty cells
- Space Complexity: O(E) recursion depth in the worst case

solutions.name: Backtracking with Boolean Constraint Tables
solutions.description:
## Approach

Precompute which digits already appear in each row, column, and box, and collect all empty cells into a list. During recursion, a candidate digit is legal when the three boolean tables all say it is unused.

## Key Insight

The search tree is the same as plain backtracking, but legality checks become constant-time table lookups instead of repeated board scans.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(9^E)
- Space Complexity: O(E) for recursion and the list of empty cells, plus constant-size constraint tables

solutions.name: Bitmask Constraint Backtracking
solutions.description:
## Approach

Store used digits for each row, column, and box as 9-bit masks. For an empty cell, compute available digits with `FULL_MASK & ~(rows[row] | columns[col] | boxes[box])`, then iterate through the set bits.

## Key Insight

A mask compresses the candidate set into one integer. Bit operations both test legality and enumerate remaining candidates without scanning digit arrays.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(9^E)
- Space Complexity: O(E) for recursion and empty-cell storage

solutions.name: Minimum Remaining Values Bitmask Search
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use the same row, column, and box masks, but before each recursive step scan all empty cells and choose the one with the fewest legal candidates. Then try only the set bits in that smallest candidate mask.

## Key Insight

This is the minimum-remaining-values heuristic from constraint solving. It keeps the same correctness argument as backtracking while reducing wasted branching on many puzzles.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(9^E) in the worst case, with much stronger pruning in practice
- Space Complexity: O(E) recursion depth
